item.content:encoded:
PITTSBURGH — Nick Gonzales has been one of the Pittsburgh Pirates' best hitters, and he could finish as one of the best in baseball.
Gonzales has hit .304/.367/.392 for an OPS of .759 in 141 games for the Pirates, giving him the best batting average and the fourth-best in the National League, with nine games left in the 2026 season.
The Pirates have Gonzales starting at third base in the series opener against the Kansas City Royals at PNC Park on Sept. 18, and it's another chance for him to finish his season strong.
Gonzales also has a realistic chance of winning the NL Batting Title, with Freddy Sanchez the last Pirates player to do so in 2006, batting .344.
Who Gonzales Faces in the NL Batting Title
NL Batting Title Leaders
| Player | Batting Average | Team |
|---|---|---|
| Luis Arraez | .315 | Philadelphia Phillies |
| Gabriel Moreno | .307 | Arizona Diamondbacks |
| Otto Lopez | .306 | Miami Marlins |
| Nick Gonzales | .304 | Pittsburgh Pirates |
| TJ Rumfield | .301 | Colorado Rockies |
Gonzales ranks fourth in the NL and is nine points behind Philadelphia Phillies second baseman Luis Arraez, who leads with a .315 batting average.
Arraez is always towards the top of the batting average leaderboards, winning three straight batting titles from 2022 to 2024, .316 with the Minnesota Twins in 2022, .354 with the Miami Marlins in 2023 and then .314 with both the Marlins and the Padres in 2024.
Moreno is having a career year, like Gonzales, and has never hit above .300 before. He's been excellent in September, batting .333/.410/.611 for a 1.021 OPS.
Lopez is also putting up his best season yet, and has bounced back from a poor August by hitting .316/.418/.404 for an OPS of .822 in September.
Rumfield has been great in his rookie season and at his very best this month, batting .408/.491/.633 for an OPS of 1.124.
Why Gonzales Winning Batting Title Means to Pirates
Gonzales has been a constant for the Pirates on the basepaths and someone they can rely on to get a rally going.
He hit his best in July, .388/.438/.544 for an OPS of .982, but has hit just .260/.352/.323 for an OPS of .675 since the start of August.
Gonzales needs to put up some great numbers to overtake Arraez and the other competition, but it's not impossible.
He's gotten more time at designated hitter than at third base, with his defensive struggles, but he's absolutely been an important part of the Pirates' offense.
"I hope he gets there and I hope he does it," Pirates manager Don Kelly said about Gonzales. "Awesome for him to be in the top of the batting order in the National League, and I hope that he can get up there and win it. He should take pride in that in how he's been able to swing the bat for us. He's had some huge at-bats, and swung the bat well and been a big part of our offensive success this year."
Dominic writes for Pittsburgh Pirates On SI, Pittsburgh Panthers Pn SI and also, Pittsburgh Steelers On SI. A Pittsburgh native, Dominic grew up watching Pittsburgh Sports and wrote for The Pitt News as an undergraduate at the University of Pittsburgh, covering Pitt Athletics. He would write for Pittsburgh Sports Now after college and has years of experience covering sports across Pittsburgh.

item.content:encoded:
Albies says the version of his teammate showing up in September is the one nobody in baseball can match.
The two have been teammates since the organization's 2015 instructional league, according to MLB.com, so when Albies talks about what his friend looks like at the plate right now, it comes from years of watching him up close.
With the playoffs only a few weeks away, his read on Acuña doubles as a read on how far this team can go.
A Bumpy Trip Through Wrigley
The week itself was uneven.
Atlanta dropped two of three at Wrigley Field, losing Monday, taking Tuesday by a score of 6-3, and falling 8-4 in Wednesday's finale before an off day Thursday.
Tuesday was the night worth remembering, because Acuña and Albies homered in the same game while left-hander Martín Pérez picked up his 100th career win, a milestone he said felt special to reach with this group.
Wednesday went the other way, as right-hander JR Ritchie allowed six runs in less than five innings, though Acuña still had two hits and scored.
The Claim and the Numbers Behind It
After Tuesday's win, Albies did not hedge about what Acuña has become again.
"When he is healthy and he gets on one of these streaks, he's the best player in baseball," Albies said.
The numbers back him up, since Acuña is hitting .339 with five home runs and a 1.025 OPS in 15 September games, and MLB.com noted this week that he was carrying a .366 average over his previous 18 games.
His season line of .257 with 18 homers in 100 games undersells him, and September is simply what he looks like when he is healthy.
Albies knows something about the other side of that coin, because he entered Tuesday in a deep slump of his own, per MLB.com, and said afterward that homering alongside Acuña felt like the old days and that he hopes the night helps him get going too.
Closing Out the East
Atlanta sits at 89-64, four games clear of Philadelphia with nine to play, and any combination of five Braves wins and Phillies losses locks up the NL East.
The next test comes on the road, with right-hander Tyler Mahle opening a weekend series in Houston on Friday night against an Astros team that just moved into first place in the AL West. Acuña has played only 100 games this season, and Albies built his answer around the health part on purpose.
Short playoff series tend to swing on whichever team has the best player on the field, and if this version stays healthy through October, Atlanta walks in with that player.
A four game cushion means the next two weeks can be about getting him there in one piece.

item.content:encoded:
The Milwaukee Brewers lost 7-4 against the Pittsburgh Pirates on Thursday afternoon, but still managed to win two out of three in the series.
They now have a quick turnaround on Friday night as they begin a weekend series on the road against the Baltimore Orioles.
Ahead of the matchup, which will feature right-handed pitcher Dustin May for Milwaukee and lefty Cade Povich for the Orioles. Brewers manager Pat Murphy announced some notable changes to his lineup, one of which includes veteran slugger Christian Yelich.
Brewers Announce Yelich Change
After sitting out Thursday and making no pinch-hit appearances, Yelich is set to return to the batting order on Friday night.
He’ll slot in as the designated hitter while batting fifth in the order behind Andrew Vaughn, who’s getting the start at first base and hitting cleanup.
Here’s the Brewers full starting lineup:
Via Underdog MLB: “Brewers 9/18 J. Chourio LF B. Turang 2B W. Contreras C A. Vaughn 1B C. Yelich DH J. Ortiz 3B G. Mitchell CF L. Lara RF C. Pratt SS D. May SP.”
Brewers 9/18
J. Chourio LF
B. Turang 2B
W. Contreras C
A. Vaughn 1B
C. Yelich DH
J. Ortiz 3B
G. Mitchell CF
L. Lara RF
C. Pratt SS
D. May SP
— Underdog MLB (@UnderdogMLB) September 18, 2026
Looking at Yelich’s 2026 Season
In his 13th MLB season, Yelich has taken a slight step back from his usual role, spending most of his time at DH while occasionally getting platooned based on the pitching matchup.
However, Yelich has still appeared in 111 games this year and recorded 66 runs, 100 hits, 11 home runs, and 56 RBIs across 418 at-bats while hitting .239 with a .383 slugging percentage and a .701 OPS.
Brewers Right Now
Milwaukee enters the weekend with the best record in MLB, sitting at 95-58 overall, with just nine regular-season games remaining.
After their series with the Orioles, they’ll finish out the season on the road against the Philadelphia Phillies for three games and then return home to face the St. Louis Cardinals.

item.content:encoded:
The Atlanta Braves are set to open up a new weekend series against the Houston Astros.
Atlanta can clinch a playoff berth with a win on Friday, and they will be looking to do so with Tyler Mahle on the mound.
Before the Astros series began, the Braves announced another Austin Riley lineup demotion.
More MLB on Heavy: Atlanta Braves Quietly Announce 6 Roster Moves Before Astros Series
Austin Riley Dropped in Braves Order Again
For a third straight day, Austin Riley has been dropped in the Braves order.
Just a handful of games ago, Riley was batting 6th for the Braves.
On Friday, he is slotted in the 8-hole.
His spot in the order has been very fluid this season between 6-8.
Here is the full Braves batting order for 9/18:
Braves 9/18: “D. Baldwin DH R. Acuña Jr. RF M. Olson 1B M. Harris II CF M. Dubón SS O. Albies 2B M. Yastrzemski LF A. Riley 3B S. Murphy C T. Mahle SP”
Other lineup changes include Ozzie Albies being dropped to sixth, Mike Yastrzemski joining the batting order, and Drake Baldwin/Ronald Acuña Jr. switching in the lineup comparable to last game, which is common.
Sean Murphy will also form a battery with Tyler Mahle.
More MLB on Heavy: Tarik Skubal Shares Eyebrow Raising Comment After Los Angeles Dodgers Clinching Moment
Inside Austin Riley’s 2026 Season
Austin Riley is the highest-paid player in Braves franchise history.
He has not played up to his potential this season, which is why he’s been batting at the bottom of the order for the Braves.
However, that being said, if Riley can have a playoff moment or two for Atlanta in October, fans will quickly forgive him.

item.content:encoded:
In the new weekly podcast, host and baseball superstar Ronald Acuña Jr. will sit down with friends, family and superstars to tell their stories of greatness
WHAT: My Cultura, iHeartMedia’s podcast network dedicated to elevating Latino voices and stories, and Rimas Sports, a premier sports management and brand partnerships agency, today announced the launch of “La Bestia with Ronald Acuña Jr.,” a new Spanish-language podcast offering fans an unprecedented look into the life, career, and mindset of one of baseball’s biggest stars.
Hosted by MLB superstar and 2025 Comeback Player of the Year, Ronald Acuña Jr. will sit down with friends, family and real life heroes to dive into the heart of Latino identity: familia, hustle, music, pressure, pride and the mindset it takes to become “La Bestia” in your own life. From childhood dreams and family dynamics to early failures and make-or-break moments, each episode will dive deep into the origin story of greatness.
“La Bestia with Ronald Acuña Jr.” is the first show from a new partnership with Rimas Sports in which the Puerto Rican sports agency will co-produce original podcasts and content with iHeartMedia’s My Cultura network. Rimas Sports and iHeartMedia are both committed to building and celebrating the next generation of Latino voices.
In the first episode, Acuña is joined by his dad. Throughout the series listeners can also expect to hear from rapper and singer Guaynaa; professional baseball players Luisangel Acuña, Gleyber Torres, Maikel Garcia and Vladimir Guerrero Jr.; internet personality Marko Terzo; mentalist Michel Gallero; and more as the Rookie of the Year, Comeback Player of the Year and celebrated hype man for Team Venezuela kicks off his show.
WHEN: The first episode is available today, September 16, 2026 with new episodes releasing weekly on Wednesdays. Fans can listen to the first episode now here.
WHERE: “La Bestia with Ronald Acuña Jr.'' is distributed by iHeartPodcasts and is available on the iHeartRadio app and everywhere podcasts are heard. Full video episodes will also be available on iHeart and YouTube.
About Rimas Sports
Co-founded by global superstar Bad Bunny and Rimas Entertainment executives, Rimas Sports is a next-generation agency redefining the intersection of sports, music, and Latino culture. Based in Puerto Rico and launched in 2023, the agency represents over 60 elite athletes, including MLB stars Fernando Tatis Jr. and Ronald Acuña Jr., padel world No. 1 Agustín Tapia, and 2025 WBO champion Xander Zayas. Rimas Sports blends talent management, brand strategy, and creative content to drive both professional success and global cultural impact.
About My Cultura Podcast Network
iHeartMedia’s My Cultura Podcast Network launched May 2021 in collaboration with Enrique Santos, iHeartMedia’s top-rated on-air personality and President and Chief Creative Officer of iHeartLatino, and has since welcomed actor, producer, entrepreneur and activist Wilmer Valderrama along with Eva Longoria and her studio Hyphenate Media Group as stakeholders. Since launch, the network has seen steady listener growth and has become home to more than 60 podcasts including hit series “Suite 305 with Lele Pons,” “Bleep! with Ana Navarro,” “Latino USA,” “Against All Odds with Yris Palmer,” “Agushto Papá,” “How Hard Can It Be? with Diana Maria Riva,” “No Safe Words with October and Tony Gonzalez,” “Soul Searching with Chiquis,” Wilmer Valderrama’s “Dos Amigos,” “Hungry for History with Eva Longoria and Maite Gomez-Rejón,” "Magical Rewind,” “Tengo Testimonio with Jorge Lozano,” “Radio Ambulante," “Enrique Santos Podcast,” and many more. All My Cultura shows are distributed by iHeartPodcasts. Listeners can find the full catalog of My Cultura podcasts here.

item.content:encoded:
The Triple Crown in the baseball world is a bit of an old-school feat, but it is a feat that very rarely happens these days, nonetheless. No hitter has won a Triple Crown since Miguel Cabrera pulled it off in 2012. Cabrera's feat was the first since 1967. A Triple Crown is leading your respective league in batting average, home runs and RBI. As noted, it's a bit old school because batting average isn't the most preferred rate stat and people have also shifted attention away from RBI.
Still, it's really cool to track when someone is close, and Astros outfielder and AL MVP frontrunner Yordan Alvarez has a real shot as the 2026 season winds down.
Heading into the penultimate weekend of the 2026 MLB season, here are the leaderboards, with Alvarez sitting in the top two of each category.
AL batting average leaders
1. Yordan Alvarez, Astros: .311 (.311444)
2. Chandler Simpson, Rays: .311 (.310661)
3. Yandy Díaz, Rays: .295
AL home run runs
1. Junior Caminero, Rays, 41
2. Yordan Alvarez, Astros, 40
3. Ben Rice, Yankees, 38
4. Pete Alonso, Orioles, 37
AL RBI leaders
1. Pete Alonso, Orioles, 102
2. Yordan Alvarez, Astros, 99
3. Junior Caminero, Rays, 96
4. Jo Adell, Guardians, 92
5. Ben Rice, Yankees, 92
As illustrated, all are tight races. It's possible Alvarez ends up leading the AL in none of the three categories, but he's right on the precipice of having a lead in all three.
Coincidentally, the last six Triple Crown winners in MLB have all been on the AL side. No National League player has won the Triple Crown since Hall of Famer Joe "Ducky" Medwick in 1937. Since then, the AL has seen Ted Williams (1942 and 1947), Mickey Mantle (1956), Frank Robinson (1966), Carl Yastrzemski (1967) and Miguel Cabrera (2012) pull it off.
No Astros player has ever won the Triple Crown.
Yordan Alvarez Triple Crown prediction
Could Alvarez become the first? The Astros -- who are clinging to the lead in the AL West -- and Alvarez have nine games remaining: they host the Braves for a three-game set this weekend before closing the regular season with a six-game road trip in Seattle (two games) and Sacramento (four games)
The two games in Seattle bring a difficult ballpark, but with three home games and finishing with four in Sacramento's Sutter Health Park, the conditions seem ripe for a strong finish. I'll predict that he gets the job done and wins the Triple Crown.

item.content:encoded:
¿Quién es el mejor campocorto en el béisbol?
La respuesta convencional en este momento probablemente sería el torpedero de los Reales, Bobby Witt Jr., y con buen motivo. El joven de 26 años es un tres veces convocado al Juego de Estrellas y ganador de dos Guantes de Oro, dos Bates de Plata, un título de bateo en el 2023 y un Guante de Platino la temporada pasada. También ha terminado segundo y cuarto en la votación para Jugador Más Valioso de la Liga Americana en cada una de las últimas dos campañas.
Sin embargo, ¿si le haces esa pregunta a la leyenda de los Rojos, Joey Votto? Recibirás una respuesta diferente. El JMV de la Liga Nacional del 2010 se unió a MLB Now el viernes y argumentó que Elly de la Cruz de Cincinnati es el mejor paracorto del béisbol.
Al entrar al juego del viernes, el dominicano tenía bateaba .284/.362/.517 con 29 dobles, 28 jonrones, 74 impulsadas, 150 hits, 26 bases robadas y OPS+ de 142 en 134 partidos. En comparación, Bobby Witt Jr. llevaba .276/.359/.441 con 30 dobles, 18 cuadrangulares, 54 empujadas, 144 imparables, 42 bases robadas y OPS+ de 126 en la misma cantidad de encuentros (134).
Votto argumentó que el estadio local de Witt (el Kauffman Stadium) favorece más su estilo de juego que el estadio local de De la Cruz (el Great American Ball Park). Ofensivamente, los números lo demuestran, ya que Witt batea .306/.376/.519 en casa esta temporada. En la ruta, sus números no son tan fuertes, ya que registra .245/.340/.360 en los juegos fuera de casa esta campaña.
Por otro lado, De la Cruz tiene .301/.395/.544 como local esta temporada y su ofensiva no ha disminuido tanto en la carretera. En sus partidos como visitante, batea .268/.329/.491.
El área en que Witt se destaca por encima de De la Cruz es la defensa. Witt es tercero en general en Grandes Ligas con 22 Outs Por Encima Del Promedio, cuarto en general en Valor De Carreras A La Defensa (16) y tiene ocho Carreras Defensivas Salvadas (DRS), según FanGraphs. De la Cruz tiene números mixtos en esas métricas, ya que tiene ocho Outs Por Encima Del Promedio (empatado en el puesto 33), cinco en Valor De Carreras A La Defensa (empatado en el puesto 62) y -6 Carreras Defensivas Salvadas.
Votto argumentó que la defensa es lo único que impide que De la Cruz sea uno de los mejores jugadores de las Mayores.
"Probablemente ésa sea la última pieza del rompecabezas [para ponerlo] en la categoría de [Shohei] Ohtani, ponerlo en ésa de [Aaron] Judge, ponerlo en ésa de 'mejor jugador del deporte' -- Pete Crow-Armstrong --", expresó Votto.

item.content:encoded:
Many fans rely on numbers to tell the story of a baseball season. For 2026, I’m going with letters. Here’s the story of the regular season from A to Z.

A: Yordan Alvarez: He’s the only qualifier in baseball with an OBP of over .400. He’s leading the American League in batting, on-base, slugging, OPS, and walks. Where would Joe Espada’s Astros be without him? Yordan is still the favorite to win the American League MVP, despite his numbers falling off a bit down the stretch.
B: Bryan Baker: Tampa Bay scored 698 runs and allowed 618 in games through September 17. That would give them a record of 84-68 according to the Pythagorean Theorem. But they were 93-59, nine games better. Credit in part goes to their closer Baker, leading the league with 40 saves this season..
C: Pete Crow-Armstrong: When the Cubs suffered through a 10-game losing streak in May, Pete batted just .161 (5-36 AB) in those 10 games. In games through September 17, PCA in 85 Cubs victories: .357/.442/.740. He scored 89 runs in 85 Cubs wins. The NL MVP by a mile. You cannot tell the story of the 2026 season without talking about Pete Crow-Armstrong.
D: Jacob deGrom: On September 10, deGrom started against the Mariners in Seattle. In six innings, he faced just 19 batters, one over the minimum. He struck out 12, gave up one hit, walked none, and didn’t allow a run. He left the game with Texas leading by three runs. The bullpen flushed away the lead and Texas wound up losing the game. The story of deGrom’s career. Jacob is historically significant. He has started 277 games in his career, and three of his top 10 (ranked by Pitchers’ Game Score) have come in 2026.
E: Errors: There’s only been one season EVER with fewer errors per game than 2026. Of course, that would be 2025. No pitcher has made more than four errors this season. In 1969, Jim Kaat won a Gold Glove, despite making eight errors (tied for the MLB lead with Boston’s Ray Culp among pitchers). Gold Gloves were all reputation in those days. In fact, Kaat’s longtime Minnesota teammate, Zoilo Versalles, won a Gold Glove in 1965 despite making 39 errors!
F: Freddie Freeman: Freeman has hit 32 doubles this year and 579 in his career. Is 579 doubles a lot? Well, that’s 90 more than the next-closest active player, Paul Goldschmidt. And when Freddie legs out his 600th, he’ll become only the 19th player with at least 600 doubles. He’s a little more than a season away from passing both Hank Aaron (624) and Barry Bonds (601).
G: Vladimir Guerrero Jr.: Vlad Jr. hit a home run every 25 at-bats in 2025. He’s hit a home run every 58 at-bats in 2026. He didn’t hit his first home run at home this year until Toronto’s 75th home game. He had gone 84 straight home games without a homer.
H: Bryce Harper: In March, Harper hit a two-run game-tying homer in the 8th inning of the WBC Finals. This season, his wRC+ (139) has been one of the top dozen in the majors. In October, can he lead the Phillies to his first World Series championship?
I: Raisel Iglesias: The Braves have spent all season in first place, and Iglesias is a big part of that. In the last 10 years (2017-2026) only one player (Kenley Jansen) has more saves than Iglesias. He’s 33-for-36 in save chances this year for the Braves. But here’s the thing: over the last five years, he’s saved 130 games for the Braves, but only one in the postseason. That has to change.
J: Aaron Judge: #99 missed 99 days (84 games) this season with a rib injury, but the three-time MVP came back in mid-September with enough time to get his timing back at the plate. Yankees fans will have to hope that the leg tightness isn’t a big deal.
K: Steven Kwan: There hasn’t been a hotter hitter in the American League since the start of July. Kwan is batting .350 since July 1, and .351 since the All-Star break. The Guardians have needed every bit of his offense, as José Ramírez has not been the same since returning from his broken left hamate bone.
L: Brandon Lowe: In his first season with Pittsburgh, Lowe has hit a career best 30 homers and has an OPS over .800. The Pirates offense was one of the big stories of the first half of the 2026 season, and Lowe was a big reason why. In the second half, injuries to Oneil Cruz and Ryan O’Hearn have sunk the Bucs but the offense was fun while it lasted.
M: Jacob Misiorowski: Milwaukee has the best record in baseball, and he’s a big reason why. Has any Brewers pitcher ever had a better season than the 24-year-old ace? Sorry, fans of Teddy Higuera. The answer is no. “The Miz” leads the majors in strikeouts (243). He leads the majors in ERA (1.89). He’s striking out more than 13 batters per nine innings! Misiorowski has had 1,053 pitches this season over 100.0 mph. No one else in pitch tracking era (2008-present) has had a season of 1,000 or more.
N: No-Hitters: On May 25, three Astros pitchers Tatsuya Imai (6 IP), Steven Okert (1 IP), and Alimber Santa (2 IP) combined to complete the Astros’ fifth combined no-hitter in franchise history. No one pitcher has completed a no-hitter since Blake Snell did it in August of 2024 for the Giants.
O: Shohei Ohtani: There are two players whose last name starts with “O” with more homers than Ohtani this season: Matt Olson and Kazuma Okamoto. But Ohtani made 14 brilliant starts (1.79 ERA) and his wRC+ of 142 is in the top 10 in the game.
P: Salvador Perez: The 36-year-old put up nearly 600 at-bats this season. And while most of them came as a DH or 1B, he did start 44 games behind the plate. In his 15-year career, he’s caught 1,427 games (1,396 starts) and nearly 12,000 innings.
Q: Quick games: On September 7, in an afternoon game at Citizens Bank Park, the Phillies beat the Braves 1-0 in a game that took 1:51 to play. On June 16 at Dodger Stadium, the Dodgers defeated the Rays 1-0 in a game that took 1:52 to complete. And in early April, the Royals defeated the White Sox in games on April 10 and 11 that lasted in 1:54 and 1:55, respectively. Thank you, pitch clock.
R: Eduardo Rodriguez: The Diamondbacks have won 22 of E-Rod’s first 30 starts. Talk about valuable! He has a 2.62 ERA this season (it was 5.04 and 5.02 in the two previous seasons). This is his best year since 2019.
S: Cam Schlittler: Is he the AL MVP, or just the AL Cy Young? The Yankees won 20 of his 31 starts. The Yankees don’t need a lot of offense when he takes the mound. He has a 1.14 ERA in 16 road starts this season! Since earned runs became official in both leagues in 1913, Schlittler’s 1.14 road ERA is the fourth best (minimum 15 road starts). The top three: Bob Gibson in 1968 (0.81 ERA); Walter Johnson in 1913 (1.06 ERA); and Greg Maddux in 1995 (1.12 ERA).
T: Bruce Turang: What a player! His OPS has gone up in each of his first four seasons. He’s now a 20 HR/20 SB/100 runs/100 RBI player. The Brewers need him to improve his performance in last year’s NLCS vs. the Dodgers, when he went 1-for-15 (.067).
U: Uncle Charlie (curveball): The curveball is heading toward extinction, much like individual no-hitters. Curveballs have only accounted for 6.4% of pitches this season, the second lowest rate since first tracked in 2008 (2024: 6.1%). That’s pure curves, not including slow curves or knuckle-curves. Want to know which pitcher has thrown the most curveballs (including knuckle and slow curves) this year? Philadelphia’s Aaron Nola, at 942.
V: Miguel Vargas: The White Sox have been one of the best stories this year, and we could have given the “V” to manager Max Venable. But Vargas’ 31 home runs and stealing 19 bases in 21 attempts makes him the choice. Vargas has a 4.7 WAR this season, up from 1.9 last year.
W: Willson and Wilyer, the heart of the Boston lineup. Right fielder Wilyer Abreu leads the American League with 36 doubles. He also leads the AL in outfield assists with 12. Willson Contreras has an OPS of .905, second in AL to Alvarez, even ahead of Rays slugger Junior Caminero. Remember, Boston was 14 games under .500 as late as June 24. And then the season turned around.
X: Xander Bogaerts: The Padres have played well down the stretch and now appear likely to reach the postseason. And X-Man has contributed, stealing 21 bases in 22 attempts this year. It’s no fluke, either. He stole 20 of 22 last season. In his four seasons with the Padres, he has stolen 73 bases in 81 attempts. That’s efficiency.
Y: Yoshinobu Yamamoto: The Dodgers’ Yoshinobu Yamamoto has a 1.98 ERA in 10 starts after the All-Star break. He’s probably the key to the Dodgers’ chances of completing a three-peat. Who can forget what he did last October, when he went 5-1, with a 1.45 ERA in 37.1 postseason innings.
Z: Zack Wheeler: From July 21 through August 24, Wheeler had a stretch of seven starts that saw him give up 26 runs (25 earned) in 31.1 innings (7.18 ERA). He was terrific in the first half and recaptured his form down the stretch. If the Phillies are going to go deep into October, they’ll need Wheeler (and their other two aces) to be at the top of their game.
Editors’ Note: Elliott Kalb - dubbed “Mr. Stats” decades ago by Marv Albert and Bob Costas - is the former Senior Editorial Director at MLB Network and a longtime contributor of research and information to NBC Sports’ telecasts.

LOUISVILLE, Ky. (AP) — Alex Bregman and his Chicago Cubs teammates celebrated the third baseman's horse winning a race at Churchill Downs.
It was short-lived, however, when the horse was claimed by new owners afterward.
Act of Parliament overcame a troubled start under jockey Axel Concepcion and rallied to win by three-quarters of a length on Thursday. The 3-year-old colt paid $8.68 to win.
"It was electric,” winning trainer Will Walden said. “To have Alex and the entire team here and then have the horse come through like that made it a pretty special night.”
The Cubs visited the historic Louisville track on their off day before opening a three-game set at Cincinnati on Friday.
Cubs MVP candidate Pete Crow-Armstrong delivered a pep talk to Act of Parliament in the paddock before the race. Cubs manager Craig Counsell led the colt into the winner's circle afterward.
Several Cubs rookies dressed in racing-themed costumes, including pitcher Ryan Rolison, who donned a horse costume, and Pedro Ramirez, who dressed as a jockey.
Bregman Family Racing, the ballplayer's stable, bought Act of Parliament for $65,000.
The colt earned $27,108 for his first career victory. But Bregman lost him in the claiming race.
Act of Parliament was claimed for $20,000 afterward in a random blind draw used to break a tie when six different owners submitted bids beforehand to buy the colt. He was then transferred to a new trainer.

item.content:encoded:
The Boston Red Sox are set to begin a three-game series against the Tampa Bay Rays at Tropicana Field at 7:10 p.m. EDT on Friday.
Before Friday’s game, the Red Sox announced a notable lineup decision involving outfielder Jarren Duran.
Boston Red Sox Announce Jarren Duran Decision Before Rays Series
Duran is out of the Red Sox’s lineup for Friday’s game. He started in center field in Thursday’s 5-4 win over the Texas Rangers at Globe Life Field in Arlington, Texas.
The Rays are starting left-hander Ian Seymour on the mound, which is likely why manager Chad Tracy elected to sit Duran, a left-handed hitter.
Here is the Red Sox’s full lineup for Friday:
- Roman Anthony LF
- Nick Sogard 1B
- Jahmai Jones DH
- Wilyer Abreu RF
- Trevor Story SS
- Caleb Durbin 3B
- Isiah Kiner-Falefa 2B
- Nate Eaton CF
- Connor Wong C
Starting Pitcher: LHP Ranger Suarez (7-4, 3.33 ERA, 130 K)
Here is the Rays’ lineup:
- Yainer Diaz DH
- Jonathan Aranda 1B
- Junior Caminero 3B
- Ryan Vilade 2B
- Chandler Simpson LF
- Jonny DeLuca CF
- Nick Fortes C
- Victor Mesa Jr. RF
- Taylor Walls SS
Starting Pitcher: LHP Ian Seymour (9-6, 4.27 ERA, 150 K)
Looking at Jarren Duran
Duran has had a rough season, posting just 0.2 bWAR and a .203/.259/.359 slash line with 20 home runs and 69 RBI over 143 games.
Just two seasons ago, Duran posted 9.0 bWAR and an .834 OPS with 21 home runs and 75 RBI. He had a solid 2025 season as well, posting 4.9 bWAR and a 114 OPS+.
Duran has especially struggled this month, hitting just .159/.213/.250 in 44 at-bats.
On the bright side, Duran has been a spectacular defender for Boston this year, posting +5 Outs Above Average.
Boston Red Sox Right Now
Before beating the Rangers on Thursday, the Red Sox lost the first two games of the series against Texas. Boston is 5-5 in its last 10 games.
At this point in the season, Boston seems locked in to the second AL Wild Card spot unless something crazy happens. If the standings hold up, the Red Sox will play the New York Yankees in the Wild Card round at Yankee Stadium.

Gunnar Henderson and his Baltimore Orioles will square off against the Milwaukee Brewers at Oriole Park at Camden Yards, on Friday, Sept. 18 at 7:05 p.m. ET. Henderson has +490 odds to hit a home run as of Friday afternoon.
What It Means
Henderson is hitting for a .221 BA, .306 OBP and .397 SLG with a 22% strikeout rate and a 9.7% walk rate. His OPS is .703 and he has scored 85 runs. In 673 plate appearances, he has hit 23 home runs and driven in 58 runs. Henderson has recorded 10 steals on 15 attempts. He had a hitless showing in his previous game (0 for 4) against the Mets.
Dustin May gets the start for the Brewers, his 29th of the season. He is 7-9 with a 4.49 ERA and 133 strikeouts in 138 1/3 innings pitched.
